componentContentNotes.y1-stat1: Introduces data collection, descriptive statistics, probability, distributions and hypothesis testing, with attention to good statistical practice.
componentContentNotes.y1-stat2: Develops statistical models, confidence intervals, tests of means, and simple regression and correlation, including interpretation and ethical practice.
componentContentNotes.y1-intro: Introduces sustainable agri-food chains, business and consumer perspectives, academic study and information literacy.
componentContentNotes.y1-management: Combines management and marketing, including business environments, strategy, customers, brands, products and value creation.
componentContentNotes.y1-sociology: Applies sociological concepts to businesses and consumption, including social change, institutions and globalisation.
componentContentNotes.y1-skills: Develops presentation delivery, self-awareness, observation and peer feedback through practice and personal learning goals.
componentContentNotes.y1-methods: Develops research questions, objectives and feasible proposals using experimental, cross-sectional and case-study designs.
componentContentNotes.y1-law: Introduces corporate, contract, liability, competition and consumer law, including relevant EU rules and basic legal reasoning.
componentContentNotes.y1-business: Introduces management accounting, financial management and financial accounting, with applications in agribusiness and food.
componentContentNotes.y1-food: Examines food quality from business, consumer and food-science perspectives through lectures, assignments, a practical and a case. Required general and laboratory safety instruction carries no credits.
componentContentNotes.y1-math: Develops applied mathematical analysis, vectors and matrices for social-science problems, supported by computer practicals.
componentContentNotes.y1-problem: A multidisciplinary group analyses a societal problem through a proposal, literature or interviews, ethical reflection and a written and oral report.
componentContentNotes.wur-MCB20806: Combines economic, sociological, psychological and marketing perspectives on consumption, consumer behaviour and social influence.
componentContentNotes.y2-decision1: Develops mathematical programming and constrained optimisation, including linear, integer and dynamic methods applied to practical decisions.
componentContentNotes.wur-DEC10306: Introduces evidence-led economic modelling, strategic interaction, information and preferences, using real-world problems and empirical research.
componentContentNotes.y2-research: Develops qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis within the empirical research process.
componentContentNotes.y2-foodinnovation: Teams combine consumer research with social and natural sciences to develop a feasible food-product concept for a commissioning company.
componentContentNotes.y2-it: Examines the design and management of information and communication systems from organisational and consumer perspectives.
componentContentNotes.y2-management: Applies advanced management and marketing theory to strategy and implementation, building on introductory management and research methods.
componentContentNotes.y2-accounting: Develops cost allocation, budgeting, variance analysis, performance measurement and transfer pricing, with an introduction to financial reporting.
componentContentNotes.y3-agribusiness: Applies microeconomic and institutional theories to agribusiness, markets, contracts, food-production organisation, policies and trade.
componentContentNotes.y3-supply: Examines the coordination of supply-chain networks and flows of goods, services, money and information, using research and business cases.
componentContentNotes.y3-finance-choice: Selected restricted finance course: Financial Management in Agriculture. It develops farm financial management and accounting through qualitative and quantitative analysis. Corporate Financial Management is the other listed option.
componentContentNotes.y2-decision2: Selected restricted methods course: Decision Science 2. It develops multi-criteria decisions, simulation, and decision analysis under risk. The handbook recommends it for a Business Economics or Operations Research thesis; the topic and methods choice must be agreed with the thesis coordinator.
componentContentNotes.y2-strategy-choice: Selected restricted strategy course: Strategic Change Management and Innovation. It applies organisational change and innovation theories to cases and stakeholder engagement. Supply Chain Design and Planning is the other listed option.
componentContentNotes.y3-thesis: The current handbook requires 102 credits of compulsory and restricted study, including all first-year courses. This 12 EC unit includes a one-credit Bachelor Assessment that must be passed before the 11 EC individual thesis. Research may be literature-based or empirical; a written report, presentation and oral defence are required. Current chair-specific preparation remains unverified.
componentContentNotes.y3-electives: Thirty EC remain open for a minor, an individual minor or elective courses.
